tia: Heads-up — found a flaky panic in the Go generator sample when token refresh and client cancel overlap. Minimal repro attached.

omar: Can you paste the tiny repro + stack?

tia: Snippet below (sample currently uses context.Background()):

```go
ctx := context.Background()
c := redwood.NewClient(ctx, redwood.Opts{Model: "tiny"})
it := c.Generator().Stream("prompt")
for it.Next() { fmt.Print(it.Value().Text) }
if err := it.Err(); err != nil { log.Println(err) }
```

stack: panic: send on closed channel in gen.streamer.push (varies). Repro: run with TTL=2s and a background goroutine that calls client.Close() mid-stream.

sam: Two quick smells: 1) Background loses request-scoped ownership; 2) auth refresh may swap transport/token source while stream goroutines are active.

sam: Short fixes: update sample to use request ctx (NewGenerator(req.Context(), ...)), make iterator own teardown (it.Close()), and serialize token refresh (singleflight/mutex).

omar: Agreed. Also add an integration test that forces concurrent refresh + cancel with -race and assert no panics and deterministic errors. Add a tiny TTL-toggle repro script too.

parity-bot: FYI: open a parity ticket if you change public API surface. See PARITY-58.

tia: I'll open a small PR updating the sample, add the test and TTL script, and file INF-3410 linking repro. I'll prototype an iterator-ownership change behind a compatibility shim. Will @parity when PR is ready.

omar: Thanks — short DX note in the quickstart would help ("avoid context.Background() for streaming generators").

sam: Also log an event when we rotate transport for auth so ops can trace when refreshes cause reconnects.

tia: On it. Thanks! :rocket:
